title: From Impressions to Performance: Unpacking the Economic Value of Digital Marketing Funnel Engagement
content: Digital marketing generates detailed behavioral data that enable firms to evaluate how customer interactions throughout the marketing funnel relate to economic performance. This study examines the effects of Impressions, Clicks, Leads, and Engagement on Performance and determines whether these relationships differ across Email, Influencer, Paid Ads, SEO, and Social Media campaigns. A quantitative methodology using secondary digital campaign data was adopted. Pearson correlation, multiple regression with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors, standardized coefficients, and interaction-based group comparisons were employed. The findings reveal that Impressions, Leads, and Engagement positively and significantly influence Performance, with Leads emerging as the strongest predictor. Although Clicks are positively associated with Performance at the bivariate level, their effect becomes negative when other funnel indicators are considered simultaneously, suggesting substantial overlap among digital marketing metrics. Campaign Type does not significantly influence average Performance, while the relationships between the predictors and Performance remain consistent across campaign categories. Overall, downstream funnel outcomes, particularly lead generation, are more strongly associated with economic performance than initial exposure and interaction metrics. The study contributes to customer engagement and customer journey literature by linking behavioral funnel indicators with monetary outcomes and demonstrating the stability of these relationships across multiple digital campaign types and providing practical insights for marketing resource allocation.
